label: Rapid pass-through
description: Money arrives and almost all of it leaves again, quickly. The account is a conduit rather than a destination. Measured as the ratio of what left to what arrived over a short window, together with the holding time between the two.
confounders: A pooled or escrow account doing exactly its job: receive, forward, keep nothing. Structurally identical and completely ordinary.
A person moving their salary to a savings account on the day it arrives.
A business sweeping its receipts to a treasury account each evening.
notes: The retained 2% is the part that distinguishes this from a sweep. A person moving their own money forwards all of it or a round remainder; a conduit keeps a commission. That is a signal and not a proof — a 2% remainder can be a bank charge — which is why the explanation must state the measured ratio rather than announce a conclusion.
